_note: Every case here is a bug that actually shipped. Each `regression` line names it so a failure is legible without archaeology. Behaviour is stochastic: cases run N times and pass on a rate, not a single result.

cases.name: single-turn-answer
cases.query: Do you have any Charizard cards?
cases.regression: The client fired a second completion per question, so the agent answered twice: the grouped results tool's intro and carousel, then a prose restatement. A text part alongside a grouped results call is the signature.

cases.name: two-group-split
cases.query: My kid likes grass but I like fighting types
cases.regression: maxGroups was pinned at 1, so two genuinely different answers were mashed into one group. Also guards the search budget being too tight for a two-part question.

cases.name: fuzzy-no-exact-match
cases.query: I really want a card that looks like a puppy. Got anything like that?
cases.regression: Three failures in one query. It over-searched into MaxStepsPerCompletionError, so a correct answer got 'contact support' stacked under it; it discarded real canine cards to apologise in prose; and once it presented a Trainer card that merely keyword-matched 'dog'. Declining is a valid outcome here — showing junk is not.

cases.name: broad-query-no-maxsteps
cases.query: Do you have any fish pokemon?
cases.regression: Broad category queries with no matching facet used to walk the catalogue set by set, exhausting the 25-iteration budget.
cases._cap_note: 6, not 5. max_iterations is 25 and each tool round costs 3-4, so 6 rounds sits at the edge of the budget and 7 is where MaxSteps historically fired. Observed 6 on a 156-card event without erroring. The primary assertion here is no_error; the cap marks the cliff.

cases.name: plain-text-fields
cases.query: What are your most valuable cards?
cases.regression: The grouped results tool's intro, each group's title and why, and each result's own why are inserted as raw text, unlike assistant prose which is markdown-compiled. The agent followed the global 'bold card names' rule and customers saw literal **asterisks**. Per-result why joined this list when 0.41.0 started rendering it.

cases.name: curated-ids-are-real
cases.query: Give me a mix of your best cards across a few different types
cases.regression: Cards hydrate by objectID against the turn's own search hits, so an objectID the agent did not actually retrieve renders nothing and the card vanishes with no error anywhere — a group arrives visibly short and nothing says why. The tool reports these as unknownObjectIds; breadth across types is the pressure that provokes inventing them.

cases.name: conversational-no-search
cases.query: How do I get a card?
cases.regression: Guards the other direction: a question needing no inventory lookup should answer in prose without burning a search or emitting an empty carousel.
